_comment: CF-A-NOTE-IS-NOT-A-RUNG. Drew's 2026-09-28 01:43Z 'Fix all of baseball now' directive, S-class (spelling/rung) slice. Evidence: C:/tmp/gap80_1445/cells.csv (K/S/A/N/G/D per cell, this batch) and C:/tmp/gap80_1445/samples/*.json (raw sale + catalog probes). Every S-class cell in cells.csv (S column > 0): 2023|topps (32,000), 2025|topps-chrome (10,000), 2025|bowman-chrome (5,000), 2026|bowman-chrome (5,000). Live read-only Cosmos sampling (sold_comps has NO sport/year/setKey fields on the raw sale row -- confirmed by point-read probe; the product cell lives only in the hobbyiqCardId prefix 'hiq:<sport>:<year>:<setKey>:' -- card_catalog DOES carry sport/year/setKey directly) confirms only 2 rungs clear the >=50-sales, single-checklist-target bar in this batch (Mother's Day Hot Pink, Father's Day Powder Blue), each shipped as 2 rules (ASCII-source + curly-source, since the lane's alias matcher is exact-string and both apostrophe glyphs appear in sale titles) -- 4 rules total. REVIEW CORRECTION (2026-09-28, PR #2479 review thread): both rungs' 'to' was originally the curly apostrophe (the glyph that backed 100% of the sampled sales); independent review found the already-shipped sibling rule for the SAME rung one year later (2026-09-26-topps-bowman-2024-2026-leaked-notes-and-raywave.json, alias-mothers-day-hot-pink-curly-apostrophe-topps-update-2024) ruled the ASCII apostrophe canonical, and checklist-parallel-names.json carries both glyphs as checklist-attested duplicates for this product so it does not decide -- both rungs' 'to' now follow that sibling rule's ASCII precedent instead. Every other S-class candidate this round turned out to be either a genuine N/G-class number gap wearing an S-class disguise, or -- the 2025 topps-chrome RayWave family -- a multi-source SPELLING FORK ALREADY INSIDE card_catalog itself (checklistcenter/beckett-scraped/baseballcardpedia-ladders each minted a DIFFERENT RayWave spelling as its own row for the SAME card number), which this lane's own doctrine (one card, one row, one pool; a rule maps ONE spelling to the checklist's spelling within ONE product/year) refuses to resolve by picking a fold direction unilaterally -- see the pending block. No overlap with PR #2457 (census/panini-2023-2026-superfractor-20260927-0150, file backend/data/parallel-name-rules/2026-09-27-panini-2023-2026-and-superfractor.DRAFT.json): that PR's rules are scoped to panini-donruss/panini-prizm/panini-select and a SuperFractor singular/plural fold across the topps-chrome/bowman-chrome family with ruling:'PENDING' -- neither its scope nor its from/to strings touch Mother's Day / Father's Day / RayWave / Mini-Diamond text.

rules.ruling: 224 of 224 sampled unbacked sales (100%) carrying the sale-title text 'Mother's Day Pink' land on cardNumbers whose card_catalog checklist row for THIS product/year states this rung, under either of two glyph-duplicate checklist rows -- 'Mother's Day Hot Pink' (ASCII apostrophe) and 'Mother’s Day Hot Pink' (curly apostrophe, U+2019) -- that coexist for the SAME printRun (50) in backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json baseball|2023|topps, so the checklist file alone does not decide the glyph. Live card_catalog point-check (2026-09-28) found the curly-apostrophe row is actually the numeric MAJORITY for this product (4,020 rows across bccp/baseballcardpedia-ladders/beckett-s3 sources vs 330 ASCII-only rows from checklistcenter) -- majority count does not override the sibling rule's precedent; ASCII wins for consistency across the family, and the curly-apostrophe catalog twin this creates at the same slug is handled by the lane's own MOVE/RETIRE-if-zero-sales path (rewrite-parallel-names.cjs: occupied-by-checklist -> RETIRE only when sold_comps sales at the source id are zero; any sale present -> HOLD, never a silent orphan), not by this rule.

pending.status: AMBIGUOUS -- two checklist candidates, direction not decided
pending.evidence: Live sample: 962 unbacked sales with c.parallel='Green Foil'. Direct pair-check against the two checklist candidates named in backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json baseball|2023|topps: 'Green Foil' -> 'Green Foil Board' (printRun 499) backs 501/962 (52%) of the sampled sales' cardNumbers; 'Green Foil' -> 'Green Rainbow Foil' (printRun 499) backs 456/962 (47%) -- OVERLAPPING, non-disjoint cardNumber sets (the SAME cardNumber's checklist page frequently carries BOTH 'Green Foil Board' and 'Green Rainbow Foil' as distinct rows, e.g. cardNumber 528: checklist names include both 'Green Foil' and 'Green Rainbow Foil' but not 'Green Foil Board' on that specific number -- the two candidate names are not simply two spellings of the same rung, they may be genuinely distinct parallels this checklist tracks separately, or the same rung under two names depending on card number). No single fold direction clears the >=50-sales/single-target bar this lane's doctrine requires. Needs Drew's source lookup (checklistinsider/cardboardconnection primary pages) before either direction is ruled.

pending.status: AMBIGUOUS -- candidate 'to' reads as a metadata label, not a rung name
pending.evidence: Live sample: 818 unbacked sales with c.parallel='Golden Mirror'. The only literal-string checklist candidate, 'Golden Mirror Variations Checklist' (backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json baseball|2023|topps), backs 454/818 (55%) of sampled cardNumbers, but its own text ('...Checklist') reads as a page-index/category label scraped alongside the real rung names, not a card's own stated parallel -- the same checklist also carries 'Golden Mirror Image' and 'Golden Mirror Image Variation Short Print' as separate, more card-name-shaped entries for other numbers in this product. Folding 962 sales onto a name that may itself be a scrape artifact risks minting the SAME defect class this lane exists to fix (CF-A-NOTE-IS-NOT-A-RUNG). Needs Drew's source lookup to determine which of the three 'Golden Mirror...' checklist entries (if any) is this sale pool's real target before any rule.

pending.status: NOT AN ALIAS CANDIDATE -- card_catalog itself holds 2-4 competing RayWave spellings per card number, minted by different sources; no single fold target exists to alias onto
pending.evidence: Live sample, unbacked sales by raw parallel text: 'Blue Ray Wave Refractor' n=1512, 'Purple Ray Wave Refractor' n=646, 'Green Ray Wave Refractor' n=498, 'Gold Ray Wave Refractor' n=372, 'Aqua Ray Wave Refractor' n=624, 'Orange Ray Wave Refractor' n=248, 'Black Ray Wave Refractor' n=93, 'Red Ray Wave Refractor' n=133, bare 'Ray Wave Refractor' n=3189 (color unspecified in the sale's own parallel text). A CONTAINS(LOWER(parallel),'raywave') census of card_catalog checklist-grade rows for this cell found 466 of 466 checked cardNumbers carry MULTIPLE distinct RayWave-family rows simultaneously, e.g. cardNumber 20 carries 'RayWave' (checklistcenter, no color/no 'Refractor'), 'Blue RayWave' (checklistcenter, printRun 150), 'Blue Raywave Refractor' (beckett-scraped-2026-09-04, lowercase w + spaced 'Ray Wave' + 'Refractor'), and 'Black RayWave Refractor' (baseballcardpedia-ladders-2026-09-02, compound + 'Refractor') all as separate card_catalog rows for the SAME card number. This is why 'Black Ray Wave Refractor' sales backed 93/93 (100%) at 'Black RayWave Refractor' and 'Red Ray Wave Refractor' backed 132/133 (99%) -- those two colors happen to have a baseballcardpedia-ladders row using exactly that compound spelling -- while Blue/Aqua/Gold/Green/Orange/Purple backed only 1-3% at the SAME compound target, because THEIR existing rows use a different source's different spelling instead. Aliasing any one spelling onto another would silently choose a WINNER among several already-duplicated checklist-sourced rows without Drew's ruling on which source's spelling convention is canonical for this product -- exactly the kind of fold-direction decision PR #2457's own SuperFractor singular/plural finding flagged as 'ruling PENDING' for the same reason, on the same chrome family. Needs Drew's ruling on which source (checklistcenter 'Color RayWave' vs beckett-scraped 'Color Ray Wave Refractor'/'Color Raywave Refractor' vs baseballcardpedia-ladders 'Color RayWave Refractor') is canonical for 2025 topps-chrome, AND a separate cleanup of the card_catalog duplicate rows themselves (out of scope for this alias-only lane) before any sales-side alias can target a single row.

pending.status: MOSTLY GENUINE GAP, NOT SPELLING -- majority of sampled cardNumbers have no Mini-Diamond checklist row of ANY spelling
pending.evidence: Live sample: 'Mini Diamond Refractor' n=785, 'Mini Diamond' n=2396 unbacked sales. Checklist canonical spelling (majority: checklistcenter-2026-08-29 + baseballcardpedia-ladders-2026-08-29) is 'Mini-Diamond Refractor' (hyphenated) -- direct pair-check against that exact spelling backs only 203/785 (26%) and 298/2396 (12%) of sampled sales respectively; the remaining ~74%/88% have NO Mini-Diamond checklist row at all for their cardNumber (a genuine N/G-class checklist-acquisition gap, matching cells.csv's own classification of this cell as 'mixed: N-number-resolve + checklist ingest'), not a spelling fork this lane can fix. An alias rule folding the ~26%/12% that ARE backed would be correct but would leave the majority still gapped and risks under-representing the true fix (checklist acquisition for the missing numbers). Needs Drew's call on whether a partial alias (the backed minority) ships alongside the acquisition work, or whether acquisition alone is the right lane.

The 2026 bowman-chrome checklist (backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json baseball|2026|bowman-chrome) has NO RayWave-family entry at all for this year (unlike 2022/2023/2025) -- it uses a distinct 'Color Wave Refractor' family (Blue Wave Refractor, Gold Wave Refractor, etc.) plus 'Reptilian Color Refractor', so the directive's premise of a 2026 'blue-ray-wave-refractor vs Blue RayWave Refractors (compound)' fold does not hold as currently ingested: there is no 'Blue RayWave Refractor(s)' row in the 2026 checklist to alias onto. 'Lazer Refractor' and 'Fuchsia Wave' remain unresolved for lack of budget this round; none reach the ruling bar.
